# Microsoft

English · [Русский](../ru/companies/microsoft.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Big Tech · International · Loop reviewed 2026-09-26

Most loops are two to four conversations of up to an hour. Technical rounds ask you to code in your strongest language in a tool that runs the code, and to test before you say done.

## Roles covered

- **AI Engineering:** Software engineer (general interview baseline)
- **AI Leadership:** AI product manager (senior to group)

## Questions reported for Microsoft

### [Inference, serving and cost](../themes/inference-economics.md)

- **Distinguish time to first token, time per output token, inter-token latency and throughput when comparing serving systems.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether user-visible delay is separated from aggregate capacity.
- **You are asked to reduce serving cost by an order of magnitude. Rank the levers and explain how you would test whether that target is achievable.**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Amazon](amazon.md) †, [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether savings are measured under explicit quality and latency constraints.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Measure cost per successful task at the required quality and SLO.
    - Compare smaller models, shorter contexts, reuse, batching and precision changes.
    - Benchmark each change and check whether the combined savings actually reach the target.
  - Read: [Optimizing inference](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/llm_optims) (Hugging Face Transformers docs) · [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google)

### [RAG and retrieval](../themes/rag-retrieval.md)

- **When would you combine lexical and dense retrieval, and how would you merge their rankings?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether exact terms and semantic similarity receive appropriate treatment.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Explain lexical strength on identifiers and dense strength on paraphrases.
    - Fuse rankings without assuming raw scores are comparable.
    - Ablate each retriever and reranking on a fixed relevance set.
  - Read: [Contextual Retrieval in AI Systems](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) (Anthropic)
- **Where should a cross-encoder reranker sit in a retrieval pipeline, and when does its quality gain justify latency?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether candidate count, recall and reranking cost are balanced.
- **Design retrieval that enforces the source system's access rights, including permission changes and shared caches.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Databricks](databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether access checks cover the full path to generated output.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Propagate identity and enforce authorisation before content reaches the model.
    - Keep permission updates, deletions and cache keys consistent with the policy.
    - Test denied access and revocation paths; citations and logs need the same boundary.
  - Read: [Document-level access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-document-level-access-overview) (Microsoft Learn)

### [Agents, tools and protocols](../themes/agents-tools.md)

- **What does MCP standardise between an AI application and an external service that a model's function-call format does not?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether protocol transport and capabilities are separated from model decisions.

### [Fine-tuning and post-training](../themes/post-training.md)

- **Choose between prompt changes, retrieval and finetuning for a failing AI feature; include data freshness, latency and total cost.**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Databricks](databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [OpenAI](openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether the intervention matches the observed failure mode.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Classify missing knowledge, poor instructions and unwanted behaviour separately.
    - Establish a prompt baseline; test retrieval for fresh attributable knowledge.
    - Use finetuning when representative examples justify it, then compare lifecycle cost and held-out quality.
  - Read: [Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401) (Lewis et al., arXiv) · [LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) (Hu et al., arXiv)

### [AI system design](../themes/ai-system-design.md)

- **Design a knowledge assistant over ten million enterprise documents with per-user permissions and a continuously changing corpus.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Amazon](amazon.md) †, [Databricks](databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [OpenAI](openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether ingestion, retrieval, access control and serving form an operable system.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Clarify query volume, freshness and permission semantics before sizing.
    - Separate ingestion and index versions from query-time authorisation and retrieval.
    - Evaluate grounded answers and test revocation, stale data and partial outages.
  - Read: [Document-level access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-document-level-access-overview) (Microsoft Learn) · [Contextual Retrieval in AI Systems](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) (Anthropic)
- **Design a meeting assistant that records discussion, distinguishes speakers and publishes summaries and action items to connected tools.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether audio processing, attribution and integration reliability fit together.

### [AI product strategy and metrics](../themes/ai-product-strategy.md)

- **How would you prioritise features for an AI writing assistant in Microsoft Word?**
  - Product case · Senior · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether prioritisation accounts for user value, reliability and workflow fit.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Segment writing tasks and identify friction in the existing workflow.
    - Compare expected value, quality risk, engineering cost and dependencies.
    - Choose a narrow first release and measure accepted, useful assistance.
  - Read: [Measuring the User Experience on a Large Scale: User-Centered Metrics for Web Applications](https://research.google/pubs/measuring-the-user-experience-on-a-large-scale-user-centered-metrics-for-web-applications/) (Rodden, Hutchinson and Fu, Google Research) · [Rules of Machine Learning](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) (Google for Developers)
- **How would you measure success for an AI feature in a Microsoft product?**
  - Product case · Senior · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether metrics connect model behaviour to user and business outcomes.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Name the user goal and an observable successful task.
    - Separate adoption, retention, task quality, latency and cost.
    - Use a baseline or experiment and guard against metric gaming.
  - Read: [Measuring the User Experience on a Large Scale: User-Centered Metrics for Web Applications](https://research.google/pubs/measuring-the-user-experience-on-a-large-scale-user-centered-metrics-for-web-applications/) (Rodden, Hutchinson and Fu, Google Research)
- **Which business use cases suit AI agents, and how would you compare them?**
  - Product case · Senior · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you distinguish the value of autonomous action from its operational cost.
- **Explain the product trade-offs in choosing a model.**
  - Knowledge · Senior · Asked at: [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether model selection considers task quality, cost, latency and constraints together.
